description: Sources the corpus watches for changes (Phase F monitoring). Baselines are updated by scripts/watch_sources.py running in GitHub Actions. A change opens a review issue; automation only watches, the maintainer judges. Index/status pages are watched (highest signal for new instruments or ratification changes).

Copyright (c)' footer replaced. ignore_patterns now cover the only RECURRING chrome: the news-widget block, its ISO timestamps, and both footer forms. Deliberately NOT ignored: the page heading and its document/compilation lists - those are the signal. Re-baselined in the same change. If UNOOSA renames the footer anchor again the widget pattern stops matching and the source re-flags: a false alarm, never a hidden change.] Heading changed 'Status of Treaties' -> 'Treaty Status', so expect_contains moved with it. NOTE: the 2026 compilation row (A/AC.105/C.2/2026/CRP.9/Rev.1, status as at 1 January 2026) was on the page in the 2026-09-08 capture and is gone from the live page; the newest compilation listed is now the 2025 edition. UNOOSA dropping a record, not corpus drift, and no file in the corpus cites it.

sources.name: ASTRO database
_note: 2026-10-14, issue #2 follow-up: ASTRO is an Angular app, not a page. A stdlib GET returns a 7,495-byte shell - 192 words of site chrome, six <script> tags, <noscript> and ng- markers - so the stored hash covers the shell and nothing else. Any change inside the ASTRO database, which is the only reason to watch it, cannot move the digest, and the 2026-10-13 sweep duly reported it unchanged. Declared render:'spa' so the monitor reports it MANUAL instead of claiming coverage it does not have. expect_contains 'ASTRO' passes on the shell; it is kept for a renderer-backed fetch, since the declaration is also what a crawl layer reads if one ever lands in CI. Until then this source is a pointer, not a comparator.
